sensitive_conditions: The same selected C1 stationary branch must be used across D; invertibility at isolated minimizers does not by itself ensure this.
Derivative bounds and inverse bounds must be uniform on the compact branch and its specified tube.
The certificate is distance to X(lambda), not merely inner objective error or gradient residual.

content.intended_use: Convert inner solution error and linear-system residual into a uniform eventual hypergradient-error bound.

proofs.full_local_argument: The graph K={(X(lambda),lambda):lambda in D} is compact because D is compact and X is continuous. H,a,B are continuous there. Inversion is continuous on invertible matrices, so the displayed M,A,N are finite. Differentiating ∇_1h(X(lambda),lambda)=0 on U gives H(X(lambda),lambda) DX(lambda)+B(X(lambda),lambda)=0 at lambda in D. Thus DX=-H^(-1)B. The chain rule gives ∇f=c+(DX)^T a=c-B^T H^(-1)a because the real Hessian H is symmetric. Fix lambda in D and an approximate pair x,q with both certificates at epsilon≤delta. Use stars for exact branch values. The x-segment from X(lambda) to x is in T_r. Hence ||H_x-H_*||≤L_H epsilon, ||a_x-a_*||≤L_a epsilon, ||B_x-B_*||≤L_B epsilon and ||c_x-c_*||≤L_c epsilon. Write H_x=H_*[I+H_*^(-1)(H_x-H_*)]. The perturbation has norm at most M L_H epsilon≤1/2. Its Neumann series converges, so H_x is invertible and ||H_x^(-1)||≤2M. Let d=H_x q-a_x, so ||d||≤epsilon. Then ||q||≤2M(||a_x||+epsilon)≤2M(A+L_a epsilon+epsilon)≤2M(A+2)=Q. Define q_*=H_*^(-1)a_*. Since H_*(q-q_*)=(H_*-H_x)q+(a_x-a_*)+d, we obtain ||q-q_*||≤M(L_H Q+L_a+1)epsilon=E epsilon. Finally p-∇f=(c_x-c_*)-(B_x-B_*)^Tq-B_*^T(q-q_*). Taking norms yields ||p-∇f||≤(L_c+L_B Q+N E)epsilon=C epsilon. The constants are independent of lambda and of the approximate pair. Since epsilon_k→0, there exists k0 such that epsilon_k≤delta for every k≥k0. Applying the pointwise result proves the sequence conclusion. Convexity of D is retained from the source scope but is not needed in this local direction-error argument.

assumptions: g is C1 and h is C2 on an open neighborhood of the graph of X over U, and ∇_1h(X(lambda),lambda)=0 for lambda in U. This explicit smooth stationary branch is a local use restriction; A2 alone is not asserted to establish a global selection.

There is r>0 such that T_r={(x,lambda): lambda in D, ||x-X(lambda)||≤r} lies in that neighborhood. On T_r the derivatives a,c,H,B are Lipschitz continuous; in particular their changes when only x varies have finite constants L_a,L_c,L_H,L_B in the specified norms.
H(X(lambda),lambda) is invertible for every lambda in D.

For any sequence lambda_k in D and any positive sequence epsilon_k→0, x_k satisfies ||x_k-X(lambda_k)||≤epsilon_k, and q_k satisfies ||H_k q_k-a_k||≤epsilon_k. No particular outer update, inner solver, or random sampling is required.
statement.conclusion: At exact branch points, ∇f(lambda)=c(X(lambda),lambda)-B(X(lambda),lambda)^T H(X(lambda),lambda)^(-1)a(X(lambda),lambda). For every k with epsilon_k≤delta, ||p_k-∇f(lambda_k)||≤C epsilon_k, hence ||p_k-∇f(lambda_k)||=O(epsilon_k). This is an error lemma for the selected direction computation, not an iteration-complexity or unrestricted Oracle Complexity result.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let p,s be positive integers and D be a nonempty convex compact subset of R^s. Let U be an open neighborhood of D and X:U→R^p a C1 selected stationary solution branch, with X(lambda) in argmin_x h(x,lambda) for lambda in D. Put f(lambda)=g(X(lambda),lambda), H(x,lambda)=∇²_11h(x,lambda), B(x,lambda)=∇²_12h(x,lambda), a(x,lambda)=∇_1g(x,lambda), c(x,lambda)=∇_2g(x,lambda). Vectors use Euclidean norms and matrices their induced operator norms. For each k define H_k=H(x_k,lambda_k), B_k=B(x_k,lambda_k), a_k=a(x_k,lambda_k), c_k=c(x_k,lambda_k), and p_k=c_k-B_k^Tq_k.
statement.parameter_domains: p,s≥1; epsilon_k>0 with epsilon_k→0. Define graph bounds M=sup_D||H(X(lambda),lambda)^(-1)||, A=sup_D||a(X(lambda),lambda)||, N=sup_D||B(X(lambda),lambda)||. These are finite. Choose delta≤min(r,1), with M L_H delta≤1/2 and L_a delta≤1, ignoring either constraint when its Lipschitz constant is zero. Define Q=2M(A+2), E=M(1+L_a+L_H Q), and C=L_c+L_B Q+N E. These explicit constants suffice.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed problem and branch satisfying these conditions there exist C<infinity and delta>0, depending only on the stated uniform problem bounds, such that every lambda in D and every 0<epsilon≤delta with the two accuracy certificates satisfies ||p-∇f(lambda)||≤C epsilon. Consequently, for every such sequence there is k0 for which the bound holds for all k≥k0. The claim is deterministic and pathwise; it asserts no expectation or probability bound.
